root_cause.text: The block layer's `bio_integrity_prep` function failed to zero the integrity buffer when the metadata size exceeded the protection information (PI) tuple size, because it only checked if the checksum type was `BLK_INTEGRITY_CSUM_NONE` instead of comparing the metadata size to the PI tuple size.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff in `block/bio-integrity-auto.c` replaces the check `bi->csum_type == BLK_INTEGRITY_CSUM_NONE` with `bi->metadata_size > bi->pi_tuple_size` to conditionally apply `__GFP_ZERO`, and the commit message states that the previous check "misses the case where PI is generated and the PI tuple size is nonzero, but the metadata size is larger than the PI tuple," leaving the remainder of the metadata uninitialized.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function `bio_integrity_prep` contains the vulnerable check on lines 98-99: `if (bi->csum_type == BLK_INTEGRITY_CSUM_NONE) gfp |= __GFP_ZERO;`. This only zeros the buffer if the checksum type is NONE, failing to account for cases where the metadata size exceeds the PI tuple size, which is the exact root cause of the vulnerability.
